Subject: GPU roster and onramp options for AetherLabs - proposal

Hi Sarah —

Great talking earlier. Based on the forecasting deck you shared and the QPS profile Kevin summarized, I put together a short set of dedicated reservation options (attached spreadsheet) that map cluster size, a reasonable minimum GPU floor, and a staged ramp we think will keep latency stable while minimizing burn during the first 12 weeks.

Attachments: aetherlabs_gpu_options.xlsx (spreadsheet, sizing tabs + cost estimates)

High level:
- Option 1 (pilot): 8x A100 equivalent, min 2 reserved, 4-week ramp to pilot throughput.
- Option 2 (baseline production): 32x, min 8 reserved, 8–12 week staged ramp with a mid-point performance review.
- Option 3 (anchored floor): 64x, min 16 reserved, phased 12–24 week activation for peak volumes + warm standby.

Notes and assumptions are on the first tab of the spreadsheet (sequence length distribution, KV cache hit assumptions, expected 95th p99 latency SLO). We modeled autoscale burst windows to accommodate traffic spikes while keeping monthly committed spend predictable.

If you want, Marcus can join next week and walk through the spreadsheet row by row and surface the perf/cost trade-offs (batching, quantization profile, cache warm strategy). Once you pick a lane we’ll hand off to Kimberly for the term/pricing and get legal started on a short-form SOW.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Tell us which option you want us to price as final — and whether you want to start pilot or go straight to baseline.
2) Marcus runs a tech call (45m) to lock performance assumptions.
3) Kimberly issues term sheet + draft reserve agreement.

Thanks —

Thanks Priyom — this is helpful and a good starting point. A few clarifying items before we lock an option:

1) Our production traffic profile: steady-state ~120 qps (95th), peak spikes to ~600 qps for short bursts (~10–20m) during business hours. Typical prompt seq length now averages 512 tokens; we expect to see longer tails up to 1,024 during some batch workflows.
2) For the baseline: is the "min reserved" number the floor we must pay for even when idle? (Kevin: can you confirm whether finance is comfortable with that?)
3) Can you confirm how warmup credits or warm cache priming look operationally if we need to add burst capacity?

We can do the tech walk-through next Wednesday (ET) — Kevin and I will be there. Also, please include a line in the terms about a one-time activation help (1-week engineering assist) — we prefer Redwood to help prime the KV cache for the first 48 hours.

Sarah / Priyom — thanks for the details. I ran a quick revision to the options with your 512/1,024 token profile and the burst numbers. Key points inline.

Option A — Pilot (lower risk)- Cluster: 8x A100-equivalent
- Reserved minimum: 2 GPUs (committed)
- Ramp: 1 -> 2 -> 4 -> 8 over 4 weeks (weekly checkpoints)
- Use case: validate latency and batch sizes with small shard set
- Notes: Good for evaluating LLM throughput and prompt tuning. Cost impact: lowest committed monthly burn.

Option B — Baseline production (recommended for initial prod)- Cluster: 32x A100-equivalent
- Reserved minimum: 8 GPUs
- Ramp: 6 -> 12 -> 24 -> 32 across 8 weeks; performance review at week 4 to validate prefix/KV cache hit rates.
- Autoscale: allow burst to additional 16 GPUs for short windows (configured with warm-standby and prioritized preemption)
- Notes: With your 600 qps spikes, this gives steady 95th latency within target assuming KV cache hit >= 65% and batching tuned to your p99 window.

Option C — Anchored floor (growth scenario)- Cluster: 64x A100-equivalent
- Reserved minimum: 16 GPUs
- Ramp: staged 8-week activations until 64 active; secondary warm pool for burst; 12–24 week full ramp for production-critical use cases
- Notes: Best for teams that need hard throughput SLAs and multi-region DR. Cost delta vs. Option B ~ +60% committed spend.

Operational mechanics (short):
- Warmup credits: we include one 48-hour engineering prime (as Sarah requested) with every baseline or anchored floor agreement. That shows up as a credit and a short SOW item.
- Cache priming: Redwood will run controlled replay traffic to warm KV caches; we recommend at least 24–48 hours of priming for production baselines to hit the 65%+ cache target.
- Decommit / stepdown: we can include a 30/60/90 day soft-stepdown window for the reserved floor if you want more flexibility after month 6.

Attachments referenced: aetherlabs_gpu_options.xlsx (revised tab "Marcus_notes"), redwood_reserve_terms_v1.pdf

If you prefer, we can propose a hybrid: start at 24 GPUs (min 6) and cap burst at +8 for first 4 weeks, then expand to 32 if p99 is confirmed. That reduces first month commit and speeds time-to-value.

Happy to discuss on Wed ET — Priyom, can you schedule 45m with Sarah/Kevin?

— Marcus Lin
Director, Solutions Architecture
Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com

Sarah — following up with pricing and the commercial outline. I’ve attached the term summary and the draft reserve terms for review.

Summary (high level):
- Option A (pilot): priced as usage-forward with a small-monthly retainer to cover reserved floor and activation support. Minimum term: 1 month.
- Option B (baseline): 12-month commitment recommended; monthly committed GPUs billed at the reserved floor rate. We offer a 6% volume discount if you commit to auto-renew for a second 12-month term.
- Option C (anchored): 24-month typical; includes SLA addendum for p99 latency and multi-region readiness.

Commercial notes:
- Activation credit: one 48-hour engineering prime included for Option B and C (we will operationally run the cache prime).
- Credits for underutilization: we can include a one-time buffer credit in months 1–3 if usage is below 50% of committed floor; thereafter standard billing applies.
- DocuSign link for baseline term sheet: https://docusign.com/session/ABC123def

Next steps:
1) Confirm which option (or the hybrid Marcus proposed) you want priced as final.
2) If baseline, Kimberly will issue a term sheet and counter-signable DocuSign within 24 business hours.
3) Once signed, we schedule the activation work week and tech kickoff.
